_meta: A sender with a burst of items to deliver to a receiver that has a bounded buffer and a fixed processing rate, used to show why credit-based flow control -- the receiver tells the sender how many items it can currently accept, and the sender never sends more than that -- prevents buffer overflow at the source, whereas a sender that ignores the receiver's capacity overruns the buffer and forces drops. Backpressure via a bounded queue reacts to overload once the queue is already full (it blocks or drops); credit-based flow control is proactive: the receiver advertises its free capacity as 'credit', the sender may send only up to the available credit and decrements it as it sends, and the receiver replenishes credit as it drains items it has processed. Because the sender is never allowed to exceed the receiver's free space, the buffer never overflows and nothing is dropped -- the sender is instead paced to the receiver's rate, sending the rest as credit frees up. Without flow control, a sender that dumps its whole burst at once overruns a buffer that can hold only its capacity, and the excess is dropped. capacity is the receiver's buffer size; process_per_step is how many items the receiver processes each step; to_send is the size of the sender's burst. These are the fixture; the items dropped and the peak buffer occupancy under no flow control vs credit-based flow control, and the step-by-step credit pacing, are computed.
